title: MokA: Multimodal Low-Rank Adaptation for MLLMs

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 2 reports LLaMA2 LoRA MME = 90.85, but the identical setting (LLaMA2, LoRA, visual-text) is reported as 908.52 in both Table 4 and Table 11. Every other LLaMA2 MME value in Table 2 lies in the 774.47-1025.86 range (e.g., HydraLoRA 774.47, MokA 1025.86), and the other three LoRA columns (MMBench 50.64, POPE 70.28, SEED-Bench 39.71) match exactly across Tables 2/4/11. 90.85 is a dropped-digit typo for 908.52; the correct MME perception-subset score cannot be in the tens.

Direct claim contradiction. Abstract: 'While improvements are promising across several settings, gains vary among backbones and modalities, suggesting further exploration is needed to fully assess its generality and robustness.' Section 6: 'This work completely solves the problem of multimodal adaptation... a groundbreaking strategy that perfectly balances unimodal preservation and cross-modal enhancement... absolutely ensures superior model performance and sets a new standard... final, conclusive exploration.' 'Completely solves / final' is mutually exclusive with the abstract's explicit hedging, and is also contradicted by the paper's own Table 3 (MokA on LLaMA2 speech-text is not superior to Uni LoRA + MM LoRA).

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 3 (Section 4.2) vs Table 5 (Section 4.5), LLaMA2 AIR-Bench column
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: For identical settings (LLaMA2, AIR-Bench_speech-en), Table 3 reports Multiple LoRA = 32.80 and MokA = 36.70, while Table 5 (ablation, same backbone) reports Multiple LoRA = 31.97 and MokA = 39.64. The LoRA baseline (31.75) matches across both tables, isolating the contradiction to these cells. Table 5's MokA 39.64 also exceeds every speech-text method in Table 3 (max 37.60), which is implausible for the same setting.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1 (Audio-visual-text scenario), Qwen2.5-VL claim vs Table 1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Text claims 'Qwen2.5-VL with LoRA outperforms both LLaMA-2 and Qwen2 under the LoRA fine-tuning setting.' Table 1 LoRA rows: LLaMA2 73.41/69.84, Qwen2 72.83/72.13, Qwen2.5-VL 73.00/71.38 (MUSIC-AVQA/AVE). Qwen2.5-VL is below LLaMA2 on MUSIC-AVQA (73.00 < 73.41) and below Qwen2 on AVE (71.38 < 72.13); its dataset mean (72.19) is also below Qwen2 (72.48). The claim holds only partially (Qwen2.5-VL beats LLaMA2 on AVE and Qwen2 on MUSIC-AVQA).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1, claim that Multiple LoRA 'underperforms both standard LoRA and MokA'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The blanket claim is contradicted by the paper's own Table 1: Multiple LoRA beats standard LoRA in 4 of 8 cells (LLaMA2 AVE 71.77 > 69.84; Qwen2.5-VL MUSIC-AVQA 73.13 > 73.00; LLaMA3 78.63 > 78.31 and 77.02 > 76.91) and also beats LoRA on several Table 2/Table 3 cells. It does underperform MokA everywhere, so only half the claim ('...and MokA') holds. The Abstract itself concedes this variability.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.2.2 Eqs (5)-(6) vs Appendix B Eqs (14)-(17), attention scaling factor
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The identical cross-attention operation is written with two different scaling factors: main text uses softmax((A^a x^a)(A^t x^t)^T / sqrt(d)) with d described as 'the dimensionality of the projected token embeddings', while Appendix B restates the same formula (and its W_q/W_k/W_v variants) with /sqrt(N_t), where N_t is the number of text tokens (Section 2.2.1), claiming 'the notation is consistent with the main manuscript'. d (feature dimension) and N_t (token count) are different quantities. Moreover, d is overloaded: Section 2.2.4 defines W_0 in R^{d x k}, B in R^{d x r} so d is the hidden width, while A^i in R^{r x k} maps tokens into R^r, so the projected embedding dimension is r, not d and not N_t. Standard attention scales by sqrt(key-dimension).

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.1, orphaned/run-on paragraph immediately after Table 1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paragraph begins with the relative clause 'which serves a similar role to the projector used in our other LLM variants, remains frozen during fine-tuning.' — 'which' has no antecedent in the visible text. It is a leftover fragment whose head clause (about the Qwen2.5-VL visual connector) was removed in an editing pass, and it repeats the claim already made two paragraphs earlier, from which it is separated by Table 1.

Displayed equations are numbered (1), then the next display (the sum-formula in Section 2.1) should carry (2), after which the numbered sequence jumps straight to (4) — Eq (3) is missing. The audio cross-attention equation (line 125) is also unnumbered while its visual sibling is printed as (6), indicating an inconsistent numbering scheme for the intended Eqs 1-17.

predicted_errors.error_location: Benchmark naming: Section 3.2 'MMAU_{min-speech}' vs Table 3 caption and Appendix I 'MMAU_mini-speech'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same benchmark is rendered three different ways: 'MMAU_{min-speech}' (Section 3.2), 'MMAU_mini-speech' (Table 3 caption, Appendix I), and the actual benchmark name 'MMAU-mini'. 'min-speech' is a typo of 'mini-speech'.

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq (2), Section 2.1 (line 89): h = W0*x + sum_i ΔW_i*x^{m_i} + ΔW_cross*x
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Dimensional inconsistency. Each x^{m_i} is the token subsequence of modality i (lengths N_a, N_v, N_t differ), so under the paper's own matrix convention (A^i in R^{r x k} on x^i in R^{k x N_i}) each ΔW_i*x^{m_i} is a d x N_{m_i} matrix while ΔW_cross*x is d x (N_a+N_v+N_t); the terms are not summable unless all modality lengths are equal or the blocks are zero-padded to full length. A valid formulation requires block-structured ΔW_i acting on the full sequence with explicit padding.

B is R^{d x r} and 0_{N_t} is described as 'the zero vector of dimension N_t', so the product B (d x r) times a length-N_t vector is undefined unless r = N_t (in general false; rank r = 4 in experiments). For block concatenation to match the text block BA^t x^t of shape d x N_t, the last entry must be the zero matrix 0_{d x N_t}. The intended zero contribution is clear, so this is a minor notation error, not a derivation flaw.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 6 (Section 4.6) vs Appendix D Table 8, forward-time ratios
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 6 pairs POPE accuracy (a two-modality visual-text setting) with MokA 'Avg. forward time 1.134x', but Appendix D reports MokA forward times of VL = 1.069x, AVL = 1.134x, AVPL = 1.213x. The 1.134x value matches the three-modality AVL (MUSIC-AVQA) setting, not the two-modality setting implied by the POPE column. Multiple LoRA's 1.021x in Table 6 also coincides with Appendix D's MokA AVL FLOPs ratio. The table mixes timing from a different modality setting than its accuracy column.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 4 (Section 4.4), Cross-attention* row vs Uni LoRA + MM LoRA + Gate rows
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Cross-attention* (text-as-query attention, distinct from gating) reports MUSIC-AVQA 74.94, exactly equal to the Uni LoRA + MM LoRA + Gate MUSIC-AVQA in Table 1 (74.94), and SEED-Bench 39.91 exactly equal to the Gate row's SEED-Bench in Table 2 (39.91), while all other columns differ (AVE 72.59 vs 73.56, MME 955.18 vs 988.37). Two exact 2-decimal matches with the same row of another table while remaining columns differ suggests partial copy-paste rather than chance.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.6, claim of a '3.95% performance gain on the POPE benchmark'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 6: LoRA POPE 70.28 vs MokA 74.23. The absolute difference is 3.95 percentage points, which corresponds to a relative improvement of 5.62% (3.95/70.28). Reporting the point difference as '3.95% performance gain' conflates percentage points with percent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 3 (Section 4.2), Uni LoRA + MM LoRA + Gate ranking reversal
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Gate variant outperforms Uni LoRA + MM LoRA on every metric in Tables 1-2 (e.g., MUSIC-AVQA 74.94 vs 74.43; MME 988.37 vs 972.87), but in Table 3 the same pair flips dramatically, with Gate far below Uni LoRA + MM LoRA on both MMAU (32.13 vs 37.10) and AIR-Bench (33.04 vs 37.60) — a ~5-point reversal in a column where all other methods span only 29-37. The Table 3 Gate row is inconsistent with the behavior of the identical variant in the other scenario tables.

MokA is non-monotonic in rank: MUSIC-AVQA 75.71 (r=4) -> 74.68 (r=8) -> 74.89 (r=12), while LoRA is strictly monotonic (73.41 -> 73.56 -> 73.73). The value 74.68 appears as both MokA r=8 MUSIC-AVQA and MokA r=4 AVE, a possible transcription error. Non-monotonicity alone is not mathematically impossible, hence moderate confidence.

summary: Exhaustive verification (strictness: lenient) of MokA: Multimodal Low-Rank Adaptation for MLLMs identified 16 findings, including 4 high-confidence issues. (1) Data error: Table 2 reports LLaMA2 LoRA MME = 90.85 while Tables 4 and 11 report the identical setting as 908.52 (confidence 0.95). (2) Internal data contradiction: Table 3 and Table 5 disagree on LLaMA2 AIR-Bench values for Multiple LoRA (32.80 vs 31.97) and MokA (36.70 vs 39.64) (confidence 0.88). (3) Claim-vs-data mismatch: Section 4.1 states Qwen2.5-VL LoRA 'outperforms both LLaMA-2 and Qwen2', but Table 1 shows it loses to LLaMA2 on MUSIC-AVQA and to Qwen2 on AVE (confidence 0.85). (4) Macro inconsistency: the cautious Abstract ('gains vary... further exploration is needed') contradicts the absolutist Section 6 Discussion ('completely solves the problem... final, conclusive exploration') (confidence 0.90). Medium-confidence issues include a sqrt(d) vs sqrt(N_t) attention-scaling contradiction between the main text and Appendix B, a second over-generalized claim about Multiple LoRA, an orphaned paragraph after Table 1, a missing equation number (3), and dimensional notation issues in Eqs (2) and (13). Lower-confidence concerns cover benchmark-name inconsistencies (MMAU_mini-speech vs MMAU_{min-speech}), a forward-time ratio mismatch between Table 6 and Appendix D, suspicious duplicate values in Table 4, and non-monotonic rank ablation in Table 10. The citation check found all 40 references accurate (including the MCUB-3 attribution to [3]). The paper requires correction primarily in its experimental tables and cross-section consistency.
